title: Book One · Chapter 59: Sunday Arrangements
story:
Mr Han comes to the green gate on Sunday morning. Ronan is washing his cloth at the tap. He turns off the water. Then he calls Mum.

Mrs Lan brings the brown envelope to the door. She holds it. Mr Han checks the writing. The flap is still closed.

“Yes,” he says. “That is my envelope.”

Mum shows him the map. She points to the boards behind the old rice shop. Then she shows him the two corner shops.

“Which shop should we ask?” she says.

Mr Han looks at the old route. “I went through here before. That was before the boards. I last came some time ago.”

Ronan expected a clear route from Mr Han. But Mr Han needs to check the new entrance, too.

“My neighbour brought it here. I spoke to him,” Mr Han says. “He remembered six and a green gate. He found both here on West Lane.”

“Did he knock?” Mum asks.

“He called out. Nobody answered. So he left the envelope under the roof. He wanted to keep it dry. He did not want to hide it.”

Mum nods. “Now we know the mistake. He used the wrong gate. But Mrs Gao still needs her envelope.”

“A neighbour has news of her,” Mr Han says. “She is visiting family today. She will be home tomorrow. She expects this money, but she can wait another day.”

Mr Han will leave for work first. Mrs Gao will return later. Mum looks at her sewing list. She may have time to ask about the gate on Monday. Mrs Lan can help her check the door.

“We may not find her door. What can we do then?” Mum asks.

“I can come on Tuesday,” Mr Han says. “I will take it back and send it myself.”

Mrs Lan still holds the brown envelope.

“Our first plan was your collection today,” she says. “Do you want it now?”

Mr Han thinks for a moment.

“Can you keep it until Monday evening? Mrs Gao may be just round the corner. We may find her door tomorrow. But you can say no. I can take it now.”

“I can keep it one more day,” Mrs Lan says. “Please write the new time here.”

She gives him a plain piece of paper. He writes her name and his own. Then he writes the plan in short lines. Mrs Lan will keep the envelope closed until Monday evening. They may not find the right door on Monday. Then he will collect it on Tuesday morning.

Mum reads the note. Mrs Lan reads it, too. They agree on the names and times.

Mr Han turns to the boys. “You can help with the map. But don't carry this money. And stay out of locked yards.”

Both boys agree. They will ask questions with an adult. They will not take the envelope out alone.

Mr Han leaves. Mrs Lan puts the envelope back in her drawer. The address note and new plan go beside it. She locks the drawer and keeps the key.

Dad checks his tools that afternoon. His first trial morning is on Monday. Ronan draws the route to Mr Sun's counter. He marks the tea shop with the red bench.

“Can I come with you?” he asks.

“You have school,” Dad says. “My work finishes at midday. Your lessons finish later. I'll tell you about work at home.”

Mum packs bread for Dad's break. Dad closes his toolbox. Dad and Mr Sun agreed on three trial mornings. There is no promise of more work yet.

In the evening, Ronan puts the maps away. He checks his tea box. His own four coins are still inside. They stay separate from Mrs Gao's money. He closes his box and leaves it beside the bed.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：collect＝领取；closed＝合上的；drawer＝抽屉；Monday＝星期一。

辅助理解：trial morning＝试工的一个早晨；until Monday evening＝到星期一晚上为止。

理解问题：

1. Mr Han 为什么没有在星期日领走信封？
2. 大家怎样明确新的保管安排？
